verdicts.note: Recorded aye on the council-imposed 0.1% criminal-justice sales tax [S7], which he campaigns on as the Justice Fund [S3][S12]. A flat sales tax rather than progressive revenue, and he also promotes property-tax relief for seniors and low-income families [S4], so +1 at medium, not higher.

Record plus repeated statements: aye on the 2026-2027 budget [S8], and a platform and statement listing expanded affordable housing, childcare, behavioral health, food assistance and transit [S3][S4][S12]. That meets the guide's 'high' definition; +1 rather than +2 because the budget vote alone is not an expansion program and he pairs it with core-services language.

Public affordable-housing funding (the $12.2 million for 646 homes), rapid rehousing and homebuyer programs [S3][S4][S12] against permit streamlining and the cottage-housing vote, a supply measure [S4][S9]. Mixed toward pole B; +1 medium.

Law enforcement, fire and EMS investment and a tax his campaign says funds deputy hiring [S3][S4][S7], set against crisis response, youth intervention and a 'fairer justice system' [S4][S12]. Genuinely mixed, 0 at medium.
His own platform calls for 'the urgent local action required to mitigate climate change' [S4]. One explicit statement; medium without relying on the Washington Conservation Action endorsement.
Sitting councilmember after eleven years on the Fife council, regional board seats, running on what he has 'delivered' [S2][S6][S12].

The cached Issues page (S3) confirms 'Lower Taxes' is the first of her five priorities, with the pledge to 'push back on unnecessary tax increases' and keep county government living 'within its means'. 'Unnecessary' softens it and she names no tax to cut or repeal, which is why medium rather than high; but a headline plank to lower taxes is the pole-A description ('prioritize reducing the tax burden'), so -2 stands. Dossier gap: line 69 does not record that 'Lower Taxes' is her headline plank, or the 'protect working families from rising costs' wording the basis quotes; the coordinator may add both [S3] so the score rests on dossier text.

'We don't have a money problem — we have a spending problem' with 'identifying wasteful and unnecessary spending' and 'lives within its means' [S2][S3]; her statement adds 'I'll ensure our tax dollars are spent transparently' [S7]. That is restraint-first, matching pole A. Her caveat about protecting essential programs and her call to prioritize road and bridge projects [S3][S7] are why it is medium, not high.

Streamline permitting and increase supply 'where it makes sense' (pole A) while protecting single-family neighborhoods from denser development [S3]; nothing toward public housing or tenant protections. -1 medium.

Accountability for repeat crime and disorder and 'enabling destructive behavior under the guise of compassion helps no one' [S3], balanced by recovery pathways to 'end the revolving door' [S3][S7]. -1 medium.

Never held public office, 'not a career politician', and frames her run as bringing voices 'absent from rooms where decisions ... are made' and being the first Indigenous woman in the seat [S2][S4][S7], against a sitting incumbent with eleven prior years in city office. That is the maximal outsider/renewal profile; her Tribe-and-business negotiations with the state [S7] are not office-holding. +2 medium holds.
